text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 1.2 total split across 4 members, so individually it's a net loss to contribute but the group benefits if everyone cooperates. The dominant strategy is to free-ride and keep everything, while the social optimum requires full contribution from all players—I'm weighing what a typical rational or cooperative choice would look like here.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns less to the contributor than keeping it privately, but more collectively if everyone contributes—making zero the dominant individual strategy even though full cooperation is socially optimal. With 10 repeated rounds, there's room to weigh selfish versus cooperative approaches.

I'll start by contributing the full 20 to signal cooperation and observe how others respond, then adjust my strategy in later rounds based on their behavior.
